traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria in docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md are satisfied: - Rule Naming: The plugin exposes traceability/prefer-supports-annotation as the primary rule and traceability/prefer-implements-annotation as a deprecated alias, with metadata and tests confirming aliasing and default-disabled status. - Optional Warning & Configurable Enforcement: The rule is a suggestion-type ESLint rule, disabled by default in recommended/strict configs, and is enabled/controlled exclusively via standard ESLint severity (off/warn/error). Tests explicitly verify that it is absent from default presets and that both rule keys accept warn/error. - Auto-fix Support & Single Story Conversion & Preserve Order: The implementation provides a conservative fixer that, for a single @story path with one or more simple @req lines, replaces them with a single @supports line, preserving indentation and line position within the JSDoc. Tests assert exact before/after code for single and multi-REQ cases. - Multi-story Detection & Cannot Auto-fix: Mixed legacy/@supports and multi-story patterns are detected and reported via cannotAutoFix and multiStoryDetected without attempting a fix; this is covered by targeted tests and aligns with the story’s non-auto-fix examples. - Both Formats Valid & Backward Compatibility: When the migration pattern is not present (only @story, only @req, only @supports, or story/req with supports but missing one side), the rule does not report, and default presets leave the rule off entirely. This ensures legacy @story/@req remain valid, and other validation rules are unchanged. - Quality Standards: The auto-fix only triggers for clearly-safe, single-story patterns; more complex patterns are diagnostics-only. The resulting @supports annotations conform to the plugin’s existing validation rules (all validation test suites still pass). - Documentation: The dedicated rule doc serves as a migration guide with configuration and auto-fix examples and describes aliasing, severity configuration, and manual-migration cases. Combined with the passing, story-linked tests, this demonstrates the full implementation of Story 010.3.
Therefore this story is fully implemented and verified by tests and documentation.
